paragraphs: Rav Pappa, son of Rav Acha bar Ada.

In Berakhot 29b [29a in Hyman], R’ Tanchum said in the name of R’ Assi, in the name of R’ Yehoshua ben Levi: One who erred and did not mention the New Moon insertion—if he finished, he returns to the beginning. R’ Papa, son of R’ Acha bar Ada, said: “This that we said, finished—” He said to him, “From where do you have this?” He said to him, “I heard it from my father, my teacher, and my father, my teacher, from Rav.” Hyman explains that he did not say this to R’ Tanchum, since R’ Tanchum was in the Land of Israel and R’ Papa in Babylonia. Rather, the academy’s members questioned him.
Hyman places him in Abaye and Rava’s time, citing Sanhedrin 29b, where he said (to Abaye, according to the Sheiltot’s reading), ‘This is what we say in Rava’s name.’
And in Eruvin 21b he said in the name of Rav Acha bar Ulla: Whoever mocks the words of the sages is sentenced to boiling excrement; Rava objected to it, etc.

notes.text: The matching Rav Papa statement and father–Rav chain occur in the checked Berakhot 29b; Hyman supplies 29a. His explanation of the academy’s unnamed questioners remains his argument.

No new primary scalar was returned. Berakhot 29b is an inherited recorded match alongside Hyman’s 29a, not fresh whole-passage or title verification. The compressed Tanchum, Assi and Yehoshua ben Levi personal-title abbreviations remain R-prime; full Rav in the heading and separate Acha bar Ulla report is preserved locally without transfer. Papa and his father’s title are abbreviated within the Berakhot quote. Hyman leaves the “This that we said, finished” statement cut off; no unquoted condition is imported. The dialogue says He said to him twice, while Hyman’s own subsequent explanation names academy members as questioners. His geography, chronology and Sheiltot-to-Abaye reading are attributed arguments, not independently established identities. All source holds remain.

Hyman’s print cites Berakhot 29a. In the consulted 29b, Papa distinguishes completing the prayer from having already moved one’s feet. The two singular “he said to him” formulas leave the questioner unnamed, and the reply traces the rule from Papa’s father to Rav. Hyman’s identification of the academy’s members as the questioners is his explanation of the scene. The consulted Sanhedrin 29b has Papa quoting Rava without a stated addressee. Sheiltot 69 places Papa’s “he said to him” immediately after Abaye’s statement and also names Rava as the authority. The consulted Eruvin 21b gives Acha bar Ulla for the separate saying and follows it with Rava’s objection.
